title: Elena Rybakina Withdraws From Tokyo Open With Neck Injury as Leylah Fernandez Advances
excerpt: Elena Rybakina's Tokyo Open campaign has ended after the world number one withdrew from her quarter-final match with a neck injury. Canada's Leylah Fernandez advanced to the semifinals without playing the scheduled match.
author: LokkeeVerse
content:
## Rybakina Pulls Out of Tokyo Tournament

World number one Elena Rybakina has withdrawn from the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo after experiencing neck pain that prevented her from competing in the quarter-finals.

The Kazakh tennis star was scheduled to face Canada's Leylah Fernandez on Friday, October 30, 2026.

However, Rybakina announced that she could not continue in the competition, allowing Fernandez to advance to the semifinals through a walkover.

The withdrawal came just one day after Rybakina secured the year-end world number one ranking.

Her decision has attracted attention because she has enjoyed an impressive season and was among the leading favourites to win the Tokyo tournament.

## What Happened to Rybakina?

Rybakina explained that she had been experiencing inflammation and pain in her neck for several days.

According to her statement, the discomfort was affecting her ability to perform at her best.

Rather than risk worsening the injury, she decided to withdraw from the competition.

The 27-year-old appeared before spectators in Tokyo to explain her absence and thank fans for their support.

She also expressed her hope of returning to the tournament in the future.

## Leylah Fernandez Advances to the Semifinals

Rybakina's withdrawal handed Leylah Fernandez a direct passage into the last four.

The Canadian player had been scheduled to face the world number one in what promised to be an important quarter-final encounter.

Instead, she secured her semifinal place without playing the match.

Fernandez was set to face Kamilla Rakhimova for a place in the tournament final.

The development provides Fernandez with another opportunity to compete for a major late-season title.

## Rybakina's Remarkable 2026 Season

Despite her withdrawal in Tokyo, Rybakina has enjoyed an outstanding year.

She secured the Australian Open and US Open titles in 2026, bringing her Grand Slam total to three.

She also won the Ningbo Open shortly before arriving in Tokyo.

Her performances throughout the season helped her secure the year-end world number one ranking.

The achievement represents an important milestone in her career and confirms her position among the leading players in women's tennis.

## Will Rybakina Play in the WTA Finals?

Rybakina is expected to return for the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells next month.

Her withdrawal from Tokyo appears to be a precaution aimed at allowing her to recover before the important competition.

However, her actual participation will depend on her recovery and medical condition.

Fans will be watching closely to see whether the neck problem affects her preparations.

## What Her Withdrawal Means for the Tokyo Open

Rybakina's departure changes the competitive picture of the Pan Pacific Open.

As the tournament's leading player and year-end number one, she was one of the biggest attractions in the competition.

Her absence creates an opportunity for the remaining players to compete for the title.

For Fernandez, the walkover provides a valuable opportunity to progress without the physical demands of another match.

For Rybakina, the priority is now recovery and preparing for the remaining major event of the season.
